# Loment 0.1.4.5 — preview

> **This is an announcement, not a finished release.** It is tagged ahead of time so that what
> 0.1.4.5 will contain is stated in public while it is still being built. The archives below
> are the toolchain as it stands on `main` today; treat them as a preview of a version that is
> not done.
>
> Each section says which half it is: **in `main` today** or **planned**.

Three things are coming in 0.1.4.5.

## 1. LomentGC — the four-tier reclamation ladder

**In `main` today.**

Reclamation in Loment is not one algorithm over one heap. Every `alloc` site is assigned, at
compile time, to one rung of a ladder, and *how much of this program's memory the collector is
responsible for* is a **number carried in the artifact**:

| Rung | What it does |
|---|---|
| `L0` | static promotion — a provably non-escaping allocation never reaches the heap at all |
| `L1` | last-use — the allocator front is returned right after the final use |
| `L2` | block epochs — a loop body that allocates and drops returns its whole region at once |
| `L3` | mark-sweep with precise roots, triggered by bytes allocated |

The ladder is implemented **twice** — the reference compiler (`tools/lomentc.py`) and the
self-hosted one (`loment/selfhost/`) — and the two must agree byte for byte. The three tiers
`choose gc_manual` / `choose gc_auto` / `choose gc_auto_alpha` select how far down the ladder a
unit is allowed to go. Potato **v10** carries `gc_ladder` = `{l0, l1, l2, l3, total_sites}`,
and **two independent validators** check the arithmetic (`l0 + l1 + l2 + l3 == total_sites`)
without reading a single line of source.

**Still being built.** The adaptive collector for `gc_auto_alpha` is in review
([#200](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/pull/200)); today the `L3` residual of that tier is
not collected. The GC v2 design (`gc_strict`, reclamation-by-recomputation, Potato v11) is a
design document, not an implementation — none of its criteria have been run yet.

The design record is [docs/210](docs/210-loment-gc-design.md); the ledger of what is claimed
and what is still open is [docs/202](docs/202-loment-014-release-gate.md).

## 2. Networking, on both targets

**In `main` today.**

The same `.lomt` source can open a socket on Linux **and** on Windows, from the same output
bytes. On ELF the calls are the Linux syscalls directly; on PE the runtime dispatches **21
numbers** through `ws2_32`. `syscall7` fills all six argument registers, so address-carrying
UDP — `sendto` / `recvfrom`, where the sixth argument is the `socklen_t` — is expressible in
the language. `tools/loment_pe_test.py` walks the whole surface by having a program connect to
itself: `socket` / `setsockopt` / `bind` / `listen` / `getsockname` / `connect` / `accept` /
`read` / `write` / `poll` / `accept4` / IPv6.

Two boundaries, stated plainly, because they are the parts that are *not* there:

* **There is no networking library.** `std` has no `net` module; you write the syscalls
  yourself. Nothing wraps them yet.
* **There is no admission gate.** A unit that declares
  `excluded "network: 本单元不申请任何 net 能力"` (as `loment/examples/demo.lomt` does) is not
  stopped from calling `socket` — the capability check compares *domain names* and never looks
  at behaviour. [docs/218](docs/218-loment-net-admission.md) is a research draft arguing the
  project should have **no permission list at all** rather than a gate; its criteria have not
  been run.

The measurements are in [docs/217](docs/217-loment-socket-parity.md),
[docs/220](docs/220-syscall7-and-udp.md) and [docs/221](docs/221-loment-pe-poll.md).

## 3. lompi 0.2.0 Alpha

**Planned.**

The package manager moves from 0.1.5 to **0.2.0 Alpha**. The announcement lives on the
package manager's own repository, [FujoJTOP/lompi](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/lompi).

## Install

| Platform | File | How |
|---|---|---|
| Linux / WSL | `loment-0.1.4.5-pre-linux-x64.tar.gz` | unpack → `sh install.sh` |
| Windows | `loment-0.1.4.5-pre-windows-x64.zip` | unpack → run `install.cmd` (or `powershell -File install.ps1`) |
| Windows | `loment-0.1.4.5-pre-windows-x64-setup.exe` | double-click |
| any agent | `loment-skill.zip` | the language guide on its own, for agents |

`SHA256SUMS` covers the three archives and the skill zip; the installers check it first. Both
install routes put down the same files.

**The Windows installer works in this build.** The silent-install bug that affected the
*published* 0.1.4 `setup.exe` — the self-extracting package launched `install.cmd` by a bare
filename, which `cmd.exe` cannot find when `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` is set — was
fixed in [#114](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/pull/114). The 0.1.4 installer will not be
rebuilt ([#117](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/117)); this preview carries the fix.
The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn once.

Installing and running needs **no Python, no clang and no WSL** — the package is native
binaries plus the standard library.

---

Loment is a **systems programming language** that compiles to native x86-64 — Linux ELF,
Windows PE, or a freestanding object for bare metal — with **no runtime and no libc**. The
toolchain is self-hosted at run time. The language surface is frozen
([docs/158](docs/158-loment-freeze.md) says what changing it costs); the implementation is not,
and this preview is what "not frozen" looks like.
